text:
alex_finance: Quick policy note for teams doing annual budgeting  procurement and finance are tightening up CapEx vs OpEx classification for software and hardware purchases starting next quarter. See the short primer: https://redwood.app/finance/capex-opex :memo:
tanya_ops: Can you summarize the key change? We're used to throwing everything under OpEx for SaaS.
alex_finance: TL;DR: Any purchase that creates a capital asset (on-prem servers, devices with >1yr useful life, or software licenses treated as owned) should be classified as CapEx. Subscriptions and cloud consumption remain OpEx. The big change: longer-term software licenses and multi-year on-prem support contracts with capitalized deliverables will need CapEx approval and a capex PO.
mike_sre: For on-prem infra purchases, does the new rule affect service contracts (support & maintenance) that are billed annually?
alex_finance: If the service is tied to capital hardware (support for server cluster purchased this FY), the support costs where applicable may be capitalized per accounting rules. If it's pure managed service (hosted infra), treat as OpEx. When in doubt, mark as "Potential CapEx" in the portal and procurement will triage with finance.
procure-bot: New tag available: `#capex-possible`  add it to the purchase request to flag finance review. Missing classification will default to OpEx but may be audited.
cfo_kate: Quick governance note: CapEx approvals follow the CapEx committee workflow. Approvals can take longer (3-7 business days). If a purchase is time-sensitive, use "capital pre-approval" so we can expedite review.
tanya_ops: What about leases or hardware-as-a-service? We have a vendor offering monthly devices for field teams under a 24-month term.
alex_finance: Leases and hardware-as-a-service are evaluated case-by-case. If contract effectively transfers control/ownership or has capital-like economics, it may be capitalized. Put full contract under procurement and choose "requires capex analysis". Procurement will request accounting inputs and tag for committee review.
mike_sre: Any change to budgeting cadence or how teams should request funds?
alex_finance: Keep your existing budget lines, but from next cycle include a flag if you expect capitalizable items. In the portal: choose Expense Type = OpEx / CapEx / Potential CapEx. The guide shows examples by category. Also, if you're requesting a PO that may be capitalized, include an expected useful life and whether installation/customization costs are included.
procure-bot: Reminder: automated audits will run monthly on large-ticket items (> $10k) to validate classification. Items reclassified after the fact will be annotated and finance will follow up.
cfo_kate: One more thing  for multi-year SaaS deals where payments are front-loaded or include large implementation fees, we may capitalize a portion (implementation costs) per accounting rules. Work with procurement to split the PO into capitalizable and service portions.
tanya_ops: Got it. Can you post a 3-line checklist we can add to team runbooks?
alex_finance: Posted in the guide. TL;DR: 1) Estimate useful life & implementation costs 2) Tag as OpEx/CapEx/Potential CapEx in portal 3) Attach contract & mark owner for review. If urgent, request "capital pre-approval".
mike_sre: Thanks  we'll update runbooks and tag upcoming purchases.
alex_finance: We'll run a 30-day pilot on the tagging flow and share findings. Ping procurement if you hit weird edge cases. :eyes:
